I hate multiplayer extraction shooters, I don't have time to get good at those to start having fun. But this single player one is fun from the start. Even though I've almost dropped it as well, I've decided to treat it as a therapy and upped the difficulty instead - on higher one you lose your equip on every death, which is a thing of it's own to get used to.

It is a generally well executed arcade shooter. There is a nice progression curve on multiple maps, with multiple tiers of gear and meta upgrades. A nice variety of enemies - which are almost all ducks with firearms, but also robots and whatever-that-it. They have slightly different AI in the right range of smart where it's easy if you don't make mistakes, and very hard when you screw up. They also belong to different factions and sometimes fight each other, which at times feels more dynamic then some other presumably dynamic game worlds. Even though all there is to it is to spawn a bunch of different NPCs and activate them when the player is in the gunshot sound range - third map at night in a storm when all the things spawn at once is just pure mayhem. The built in randomness of enemy spawns also adds to the experience with each run feeling different.

It does get a little repetitive and stretchy closer to the end, since it's also based on random chance for most of the loot and some quests or upgrades expect you to find certain items that might just not RNG. But the process of doing runs for those items is still fun in terms of gameplay, so I don't mind it too much.

I'm writing this on 100% achievements, so if there are ever DLCs to this (as long if it's not just new guns), that would be worth getting because of the polished gameplay base they have here. 

And judging by some placeholders that they have in the game, there would be more content to it, which I'm pretty stoked about.

The initial couple of maps feel a bit small, but the third map is huge and way more interesting which I kind of wish happened earlier in the game.  There's a variety of quests to take on so it's not just simply looting and extracting, but a lot of them are pretty much fetch quests or taking out certain enemies with specific weapons.  Overall a fun game, maybe a bit more simple than expected, but ended up the game on a pause as the devs work out balancing.  Looking forward to getting back to it later.

I like this game quite a bit. In fact, I highly recommend it. The game loop is fantastic and the early to mid game is so fun and rewarding. But once you get to Jlabs, it becomes considerably less fun and more of a grind. Specifically, the chore of finding keys; it is not obvious where or how to find them and you must search reddit for the answers from people who stumbled upon them. The quests and base building also stagnate/drop off once you get to Jlabs, which makes the game feel empty as you soullessly search through boxes and crates hoping to find something new and useful. A lot of this can be fixed by adding more quests, more items, more NPCs, more base building opportunities, increasing the drop rate of rare items and keys late game, adding more environmental events, etc. 

This review is just my opinion on what the devs can do to take it from great to legendary. <3 Thanks so much for making this awesome game. I can't wait to see how you improve it in the future!

🦆 Escape from Duckov | 👍 Highly Recommended | ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5 Ducks)

=== TL;DR ===
🦆 A deceptively cute but surprisingly deep extraction-style action game that can be brutal — or comfortably approachable — thanks to a freely adjustable difficulty setting. Smart genre blending, satisfying loot, and ducks everywhere make this an absolute blast.

=== What this game is ===
🎮 Escape from Duckov is a genre-blending experience that mixes extraction-shooter tension with action-adventure and hack n’ slay combat — all wrapped in an adorable duck-themed world.

While Duckov can be ruthless, it also respects the player’s time and skill level: difficulty can be adjusted freely, making the game accessible whether you’re looking for a relaxed loot run or a high-stakes challenge. Beneath the cute exterior lies a game with real depth and flexibility.

=== Gameplay ===
⚔️ Core loop: explore dangerous areas → fight enemies → collect loot & mods → solve puzzles → extract (hopefully alive).

Combat is fast and rewarding, with difficulty that scales to your preference. You can dial things up for tense, punishing runs or tone it down to focus on exploration and progression. This flexibility makes Duckov welcoming to newcomers while still offering plenty of challenge for experienced players.

=== What it does well ===
🦆 Ducks, ducks, and more ducks: Ducks are everywhere, adding goofy charm and humor even during intense combat moments.

🧠 Clever genre mix: Extraction mechanics blend seamlessly with hack n’ slay-style combat, creating a fresh, high-energy experience that doesn’t feel locked into a single genre.

💎 Loot & exploration: New weapons, mods, and secrets are consistently rewarding to find, whether earned through combat or discovered in hidden corners of the world.

=== Where it falls short ===
⚠ Repetitive quests: Some objectives rely heavily on specific kill conditions, which can feel grindy over time.

⚠ Movement speed: Traversal can feel sluggish in larger areas; movement upgrades or a faster sprint would improve overall flow.

⚠ No native controller support: A community mod exists, but native support would greatly improve comfort and accessibility.

=== Who should play ===
✅ Fans of loot-driven or extraction-style games
✅ Players who enjoy adjustable difficulty and flexible challenge
✅ Anyone who wants tension without forced hardcore punishment
✅ Duck enthusiasts 🦆

🚫 Players who strongly prefer controller-only gameplay (for now)

=== Final verdict ===
🏁 Escape from Duckov strikes an excellent balance between challenge and accessibility. It can be tough when you want it to be — and relaxed when you don’t — all while delivering satisfying combat, rewarding exploration, and a surprising amount of depth beneath its cute, duck-filled surface.
